t: Look up at Queen Anne's Mansions, a former block of flats on Petty France, between St James's Park and the Underground station. In 1873 Henry Alers Hankey bought the site, acted as his own architect, and built it with his own labour. It rose to twelve storeys, later fourteen, making it the tallest residential building in Britain. Sir Philip Edmond Wodehouse, a British colonial administrator who lived from 1811 to 1887, died here, which tells you the building drew distinguished residents.
